0|ef1820f9be27b6ad158f433ab38002ab8131db4d|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"NFSv4: Don't try to recover NFSv4 locks when they are lost.
When an NFSv4 client loses contact with the server it can lose any
locks that it holds.
Currently when it reconnects to the server it simply tries to reclaim
those locks.  This might succeed even though some other client has
held and released a lock in the mean time.  So the first client might
think the file is unchanged
column2: but it isn't.  This isn't good.

column1: If
column3: the locks cannot be claimed because some

column1: other client still holds the lock
column2: then we get a message in the kernel

column1: logs
column2: but the client can still write.  So two clients can both think

column1: they have a lock and can both write at the same time.  This is equally
not good.
There was a patch a while ago
http://comments.gmane.org/gmane.linux.nfs/41917
which tried to address some of this
column2: but it didn't seem to go

column1: anywhere.  That patch would also send a signal to the process.  That
might be useful but for now this patch just causes writes to fail.
For NFSv4 (unlike v2/v3) there is a strong link between the lock and
the write request so we can fairly easily fail any IO of the lock is
gone.  While some applications might not expect this
safer than allowing the write to succeed.
Because this is a fairly big change in behaviour a module parameter
recover_locks""
column2: is introduced which defaults to true (the current

column1: behaviour) but can be set to ""false"" to tell the client not to try to
recover things that were lost.
